findings.reason: naming the existing parser reframes the node from "write a reader" to "extend the reader to keep every period", and stops a second `unifiedWindows` contract drifting from the first.
findings.text: §5 opens on the premise "Reckon reads neither" the provider's `unifiedWindows` clocks; `reckon/_backends.py::budget_from_rate_limit_info` (landed 2026-09-15, commit b3977b3a7) already parses exactly that structure and reads each window's `utilization` and `resetsAt`, binding to the furthest-through window and discarding the rest, so the premise is false and the plan cites no search of it

findings.reason: extend the owner so one parser serves both the budget fence and the windowed-clocks reader rather than two that can disagree about what a period contains.
findings.text: a second `unifiedWindows` parser beside the one owned by `reckon/_backends.py::budget_from_rate_limit_info` (line 1105)

findings.reason: the plan should add the bookend reserve and the review/verify exemption to `budget.effective_ceiling` so dispatch carries one role-ceiling computation, not two that a reader cannot reconcile.
findings.text: `role_ceiling_pct` computes "window ceiling minus reserves, with a purpose exemption", the same computation `reckon/budget.py::effective_ceiling` + `withheld_reserves` (landed 2026-08-12, commit 6a0e3c9cf) already perform on `utilisation_ceiling_pct` and per-purpose reserves in the same `budget` block; the plan forks a second role→ceiling path keyed by a new `bookend_reserve_pct`

findings.reason: the plan must either justify the wrapper or fold it into the owner; a parallel ceiling with no such justification is the fork the item exists to catch.
findings.text: `role_ceiling_pct` is a thin layer over the existing per-purpose ceiling and does not say why `effective_ceiling` cannot be extended with a third labelled reserve

findings.reason: the age gate and the view-time call site are a real addition over `state_for`'s unconditional re-probe, so this is not a pure duplicate, though §5b should cite the owner it parallels.
findings.text: `resolve_configured_reading` re-implements the recorded-versus-live resolution `reckon/budget.py::state_for` already performs (recorded reading is the base; a known live probe wins because it describes now; an unreadable probe changes nothing) and reads the same `evidence_shelf_life_minutes` key `budget.availability_probe_cache_seconds` already bounds by

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — each new module (`pace.policy`, `bar.recommend`, `budget_group.group_figures`, `window_reading.read_windows`) is one entry point hiding a record shape and its arithmetic, an interface smaller than what it hides; no spread of shallow wrappers over one machinery.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — `reckon/crew/reserve.py` forks the role-ceiling owner `reckon/budget.py`, and `reckon/crew/window_reading.py` forks the `unifiedWindows` parser in `reckon/_backends.py`.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan adds a `unifiedWindows` reader and a role ceiling without citing the two mechanisms that already read a provider window and already resolve a role ceiling (`reckon/_backends.py::budget_from_rate_limit_info`, `reckon/budget.py::effective_ceiling`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — `reckon/crew/reserve.py::role_ceiling_pct` re-derives the per-purpose ceiling `budget.effective_ceiling` already computes and states no reason that mechanism cannot carry a third reserve.
